method: After freezing the pair, returned to Appendix 1, Articles 4.2 and 5.3 and the university curriculum and catalogues. Independently reconstructed the credit load, elective order, mandatory project prerequisites and thesis threshold. Reconsidered underlying UCR descriptions, profiles and offerings for the three organising concepts, including practical computing infrastructure, health evidence, language and cognition. findings: The English full-time Maastricht bachelor is illustrated using the 2025–26 rules. Year 1 has twelve 4 EC courses and two 6 EC projects. Year 2 has eleven 4 EC core courses, one 4 EC elective and two 6 EC projects. Year 3 has six 4 EC electives, one 6 EC project, three 4 EC core courses and an 18 EC thesis. The groups total 60 EC each, with semester projects counted once. The Year 2 elective follows Appendix 1 order: Introduction to Image and Video Processing precedes Game Theory in the regulations, while the catalogue order differs. The standard route includes the Year 3 project and open electives under Appendix 1, with three per period and the 15 EC maximum per period. Repeat or equivalent electives should not add duplicate credit. Exchange, honours and educational minor routes are alternatives.

Project 1-2 requires two of Discrete Mathematics, Calculus, Procedural Programming and Objects in Programming. Project 2-1 requires Project 1-1 and two of Procedural Programming, Objects in Programming and Data Structures & Algorithms. Project 2-2 additionally requires Project 1-2. Both Year 2 projects require registration for or completion of at least three programme courses in the respective semester. Project 3-1 requires Project 2-1 and registration for or completion of three Year 3 semester-one courses. Year 2 exams require 45 first-year EC. Year 3 exams require 60 first-year and 40 second-year EC. The thesis requires those credits and at least 138 overall. With 150 EC by the start of the last semester, the example can meet these gates on time. Project meetings and skills participation are part of the projects. The current programme page corroborates the broad elective and year progression structure. No current component-level regulatory claim is made.

The three 24-course plans share data and AI foundations but differ in sustained technical methods, medical data and evidence, or cognition and language. Psycholinguistics fits after the brain gateway, the health plan preserves anatomy and physiology before disease mechanisms, and the closest plan retains experimental design after adding computing infrastructure. Image and Video Processing is directly related to UCR computer vision, and the separate thesis and staged project limitations remain visible.
